what: 72 dish and wine pairs on which the benchmark label and the S8 engine disagreed, judged blind by an independent reviewer who saw neither the label nor the engine level (only dish card and wine card). No label was changed.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: High-acid sparkling with no tannin is sound with saffron fish stew and rouille, even if Provence rosé is the regional classic.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Nebbiolo has a real affinity with morels and veal, but tannin 5 is heavy-handed for a delicate cream sauce that wants white Burgundy or Vin Jaune.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: The weight suits a marrow-rich braise, but the tannin is firm for veal and the acidity is modest; a northern Italian red is the natural choice.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: A sweetish, creamy, spiced sauce makes dry, firmly tannic Sangiovese taste hard and bitter; this wants an off-dry white or soft fruity red.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Sweet hoisin strips a dry, oaky, moderate-acid Chardonnay, and the dish calls for Pinot Noir or an off-dry aromatic white.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: Mature Tempranillo with moderate tannin and hard sheep or cow cheeses is a recognised classic.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: The acidity copes with the tomato, but lean mineral Chablis has no flavour link to a sun-ripe Provençal vegetable stew.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: The red-wine sauce with bacon and mushrooms can carry a red, but full-bodied tannin-5 Cabernet is too much for chicken where Burgundy is the classic.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: A full-bodied, tannin-free white matches the meaty weight of seared tuna with nothing working against it.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: Crisp, herbal, peppery Grüner cuts the fried chickpea and echoes the herbs; a textbook vegetable-friendly match.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: Cru Beaujolais with smoked sausage and potato is a charcuterie classic: juicy fruit, fresh acidity and low tannin against fat and smoke.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Bubbles and high acidity handle lemon, garlic, tahini and fried bites across a mixed mezze table.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Sweet enough, but a 20% nutty, oxidative, full-bodied tawny flattens delicate fresh strawberries that want Moscato or Brachetto.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Ripe Cabernet suits the beef and tolerates the sweet carrot-onion mash, but it is weightier than this humble dish needs.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: Earthy red Burgundy with truffle is a recognised match, and the moderate tannin and fresh acidity suit buttery pasta.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Bubbles suit fried rice, but bone-dry Brut Nature has no sweetness to meet kecap manis and sambal heat.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: Peppery northern Rhône Syrah with grilled beef, fat and melted cheese is structurally spot on.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: A tannin-free, fresh, chilled rosé is exactly what chili-hot tomato sauce wants.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: Nutty hard cheeses such as Comté and aged Gouda with rich white Burgundy is a recognised classic, often better than red.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: The acidity matches the tomato and cuts the mozzarella, but an austere Chablis is not what a pizza calls for.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: The acidity suits the tomato and the beef absorbs some tannin, but tannin 4 against chili heat is not ideal; a riper, softer red is better.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Lamb has the fat and protein for it, but raisined high-alcohol Amarone is heavier than a roast leg wants; Bordeaux or Rioja is the classic.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Duck with a sweet-sour cherry sauce wants Pinot Noir; a dry oaky white with moderate acidity clashes with the fruit sauce.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: Dry rosé with spiced tomato, peppers and egg is a natural: fresh acidity, no tannin, Mediterranean affinity.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Red-wine sauce licenses a red and the tannin is moderate, but an oak-aged Reserva is heavier than the light Pinot or Loire red the dish wants.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: Alsace Pinot Gris with smoked pork, potato and cabbage-family greens mirrors the choucroute classic; body and a touch of sugar suit smoke and salt.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: The hint of sweetness sits fine with carrot and onion and the beef takes the tannin, but Amarone outweighs a simple mash with boiled beef.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: The herbal lime notes echo the curry and there is no tannin, but a bone-dry lean wine lacks the fruit sweetness to cushion heat and coconut.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Clean and tannin-free with fish, but light and dry against a sweet, umami-rich miso glaze that wants more body or a little sugar.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Beef fat and protein can take the tannin, but the wine's austerity and acidity sit awkwardly with ketchup, pickles and a soft bun.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: The high acidity cuts the tuna mayonnaise and the sugar handles the salt, but an off-dry featherweight Riesling is not the dry Piedmont white the dish wants.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Bubbles work with fried noodles and peanuts, but zero-dosage dryness turns austere against the sweet tamarind sauce.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Aged hard cheeses such as Parmigiano and Castelmagno have the fat, salt and protein for Barolo; a Piedmontese classic.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: The herbs and lime echo Sauvignon Blanc and the weight is right, but spiced beef broth with wine is serviceable rather than a match to seek out.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Melted cheese wants a crisp neutral white; a firmly tannic red turns bitter and heavy against fondue.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Grüner Veltliner is the classic vegetable wine, with the acidity for tomato and peppery herbal notes for the stewed vegetables.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Long-braised beef with Amarone is a recognised match; richness, spice and weight line up.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: A light, juicy, low-tannin Gamay with fresh acidity suits spiced tomato and egg.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: Skin-contact white with its light grip and nutty, savoury notes is a well-established match for tahini and fried chickpea.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: Grüner's green peppery notes suit kale and its acidity cuts the fatty smoked sausage, in the Austrian sausage-and-cabbage tradition.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: Orange wine's texture and savoury character bridge the many flavours of a mezze spread; a recognised modern pairing.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Ideal for the steak but too tannic and heavy for the lobster, so it only serves half the plate.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Pinot's moderate tannin and acidity can work with grilled beef, but the sweet marinade, gochujang and kimchi trample a fine Burgundy.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: Rich white Burgundy with buttery truffle pasta is a recognised luxury match.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: A rich, gelatinous northern Italian braise carries Amarone's weight, and the pairing is a regional standard.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: Ripe, full Malbec with grilled beef and cheese is a classic burger wine.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: The acidity cuts egg and guanciale fat, but a body-1 Muscadet is on the thin side for the richness and the pecorino.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: The nutty, lightly tannic, savoury character of a macerated white sits well with aged hard cheeses.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Fresh and clean with enough acidity for the tomato, but a saline, peachy Atlantic white has no real link to the dish.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: A red-wine braise with bacon and mushrooms wants red Burgundy; an oaky dry white is at odds with the sauce.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Dry sparkling with saffron rice and shellfish is sound and mirrors the local Cava habit.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Buttery Chardonnay mirrors hollandaise and egg; a recognised richness-with-richness brunch match.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: Savoury Tempranillo with moderate tannin suits a meat ragù, with nothing working against it.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: Crisp, saline, citrusy Albariño matches lemon, garlic and chickpea across the mezze.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Dry sparkling with raw beef, yolk, capers and mustard is a brasserie classic; acidity and bubbles cut the richness.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Braised beef welcomes Nebbiolo, but the sweet carrot-and-onion mash makes tannin 5 and acid 5 taste harder.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: Truffle pasta with Nebbiolo is the Piedmontese classic.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: No clash, but a light aromatic coastal white misses the earthy, creamy register that wants Chardonnay, Pinot Noir or Nebbiolo.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: Juicy chilled Gamay is a recognised burger wine: acidity for the fat, fruit for the condiments, little tannin.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: The bubbles cut butter and egg, but zero-dosage austerity is less kind to asparagus than a soft Pinot Blanc or Silvaner.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: A low-tannin, fresh, fruity red is the right kind of red for chili-hot tomato sauce.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: Sangiovese with Pecorino and Parmigiano is a Tuscan classic; fat and salt tame the tannin.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Acidity for the tomato and freshness for the cheese, but not a wine one reaches for with pizza.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Tannin 5 and very high acidity amplify chili heat and turn bitter.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: The peppery Syrah and the beef fit, but tannin 4 is exposed by the chili heat; a riper, softer red or an aromatic white is safer.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Slow-braised beef with Barolo follows the brasato classic; the meat's richness absorbs the tannin.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Eggs and Champagne is a brunch classic, and the high acidity matches the tomato.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: Dry rosé with falafel and tahini is a standard, structurally sound Mediterranean match.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: The body matches the mash and the oak meets the smoke, but the moderate acidity and fine detail are wasted on fatty sausage and bitter kale.

pairs.label: good
pairs.why: Provence rosé with mezze is a recognised classic.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Excellent with the steak, but the firm tannin overwhelms the lobster; a compromise rather than a match.

pairs.label: poor
pairs.why: Lamb suits Nebbiolo, but tannin 5 against chili and heavy spice turns hot and bitter.
